key_findings: Core Quadrupole Deformation Masking Limit: MR and AMR shears bands cannot form in nuclei with beta2 > 0.25 (e.g., 160Dy) because massive collective core rotation overwhelms particle shears torque.

Isovector Dipole Cancellation: E1 transition strength cannot serve as an octupole proxy across isotopes; 144Ba and 146Ba share identical B(E3)=48 W.u., but B(E1) in 146Ba is suppressed by a factor of 21 due to destructive droplet-shell interference.

Multipole Mixing Ratio Branch Ambiguity: Phenotypic energy staggering cannot confirm wobbling; in 135Pr, adopting delta=-1.6 without linear polarization created a false-positive wobbler, disproven by Lv 2022 (delta=-0.19, 96.5% M1 shears band).
Spherical Vibrator to Shears Breakdown: In 110Cd, the low-spin harmonic quadrupole vibrator abruptly breaks down at I>=16+ into an AMR double shears system, stabilized by core rotation inertia.

Shears Blade Reopening at Band Crossings: In 197Pb, alignment of additional quasiparticles reopens the shears angle, causing B(M1) to jump non-monotonically, disproving universal monotonic B(M1) decrease.
